interfaces.md: "A class or struct that implements an interface must provide implementations for all declared members (unless the interface provides a default implementation)." The ledger keeps the condition; the lesson (section 7) and quiz q3 explanation drop it: "a class must provide every method of the interface it implements". C# 14 supports default interface members, so the unconditional form is too strong.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `FakeOrderRepository` in `DonHang.Tests`: it implements `IOrderRepository` too, and a class must provide every method its interface declares without a body — as all four here do. That is the cost of a new repository method — every implementation grows with it — and the reason to keep the interface small.

claim_verdicts.evidence: single-split-queries.md: "When working against relational databases, EF loads related entities by introducing JOINs into a single query." and "EF Core uses single query mode by default in the absence of any configuration." Repo @ stage-1 has no UseQuerySplittingBehavior/AsSplitQuery (git grep -i split: no EF hits); ServiceCollectionExtensions only calls UseNpgsql(connectionString).

Definitional: restates the glossary/outline definition of repository and describes IOrderRepository as it exists; no behaviour, number or syntax asserted. Stated in the lesson as what a repository does, not as a universal rule.
OrderService.cs @ stage-1: `var order = await repository.FindAsync(orderId) ?? throw new KeyNotFoundException($"order {orderId} not found");`

OrdersController.cs @ stage-1: ctor `(OrderService orderService, IOrderRepository repository)`; Get: `var order = await repository.FindAsync(id);`; List: `var orders = await repository.ListByCustomerAsync(customerId);` — neither calls orderService. Next lesson's outline item 2 covers "`Get`/`List` read through the repository without a service", so the forward reference holds.
